newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Aznar-scope for rate cuts if CPI moderates. [CORRECTED 11:35 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Spain's Aznar-scope for rate cuts if CPI moderates. [CORRECTED 11:35 GMT]

text.p: Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar said there would be scope for further interest rate cuts if inflation moderates.

"We have already lowered our estimate for 1997 inflation to 2.2 percent and some see it below two percent at the end of the year. If this occurs, in a stable international environment, there will be margin for further reductions, although this is a matter for the Bank of Spain," Aznar said.
His comments were carried in an interview with daily Expansion (corrects from Financial Daily) published on Tuesday. Part of the interview, conducted on Friday, was published on Monday.
Aznar said he sees no danger of what he called a financial bubble, despite sharp gains in the bourse this year.

"I don't see the danger of a financial bubble," Aznar told the newspaper. "Savings will have greater attraction all the time and I am convinced that the number of companies that decide to go to the bourse will grow."
Aznar rejected criticism the recent labour market reform, which took effect mid-May, was lukewarm.

"The reforms don't take place in a laboratory as an experiment. They are applied on living social bodies and one has to keep in mind the capacity for compromise and the effects that are provoked," Aznar said.
"I resisted a more ambitious labour reform, because the value of the accord is very important," he said.
